add_attachment.description: Copy a file the person attached in the chat into the project, byte for byte: any kind (a logo as PNG, JPG or SVG, a photo, an icon, a font, a PDF, data as CSV or JSON), up to 10 MB. Use its id from its <attachment id="…"> tag, and a path where the stack serves files from, keeping the file's extension, such as 'static/logo.png' (SvelteKit) or 'public/logo.png' (Vite, React, Vue, Astro), then reference it from the code by that served path.

path.description: Where it goes in the project, e.g. 'static/logo.png'

add_reminder.description: Set a reminder for the user.

due_at.description: ISO 8601 date and time with the user's offset

title.description: What to remind them of, short

app_status.description: Whether the published app is running, at which address, and how its latest publishes went.

environment.description: production unless the person named another.

approve_version.description: Record that the person approved a preview version, when they said so in this chat. Quote their latest message's words exactly in quote; it is refused when their latest message doesn't contain them. Never call it on your own judgement or on an unclear reply: ask instead.

note.description: Anything they asked for with the approval, in a sentence

quote.description: The words of their latest message that approve it, exactly as they wrote them

version.description: The preview version they approved; the newest when they didn't name one

ask_agent.description: Ask another crew member a question when you're working on the same thing and need to make sure, instead of guessing: e.g. ask planning what was agreed with the person, coding what it built, money what was logged. They answer from this chat and their own work, and the exchange shows in the chat. Ask the person (ask_user) for what only they can decide.

question.description: One clear question, with what they need to answer it

ask_user.description: Ask the person something you need to know before you act, as a card in the chat with answers they can tap (and room for their own). Use it whenever the request is missing a detail you can't sensibly assume (when, how much, which one, one-time or repeating), instead of guessing. Put everything you need to know into this one call, the most important question first: the card shows the questions one at a time with Next, and the person sends all the answers together. Never ask again in a later turn for something you could have asked here; only a question that depends on these answers waits for them. Each question has 2-5 short options (add a one-line detail where a label alone isn't clear, e.g. what a design direction looks like). Skip what they already told you, and never ask the same thing twice. Your turn ends here; their answers arrive as their next message. Call it on its own, not alongside other tools, and don't repeat the questions in your reply. Mark the one option you would pick yourself with recommended: true, at most one per question and only where you have a real reason; if the person skips, that answer is used. Add a short helper line under a question where it needs context (who it is for, what you already know).

intro.description: One short line before the questions, optional

questions.description: Every question you need answered now, the most important first

helper.description: One short line under the question giving it context, optional

multiple.description: true when several options can be picked

recommended.description: true on the one option you suggest; at most one per question

calendar_add_event.description: Add an event to the user's primary Google Calendar. Times are RFC 3339 with the user's offset. Attendees get an invitation. The user approves it first.

calendar_events.description: List events on the user's primary Google Calendar between two times (RFC 3339).

cancel_background_task.description: Cancel a pending or running background task by its task_id.

task_id.description: The UUID of the background task to cancel

cancel_reminder.description: Cancel an active reminder by id. Call list_reminders first if you don't already know the id.

reminder_id.description: The reminder's id, from a prior list_reminders call

complete_reminder.description: Tick a reminder off as done.

complete_task.description: Call this when you are done helping with this task, whether it succeeded or the user wants to stop.

create_agent.description: Add a new member to the person's own crew, for a task they want an agent for. Call find_tools first and pass the names of the tools that fit. The member is theirs alone; their plan may limit how many they can have.

name.description: A short name, unlike any crew member's (at most 40 characters)

role.description: Its job in one sentence (at most 200 characters)

soul.description: Optional soul.md: who it is and how it works, in markdown

tools.description: Tool names from find_tools; may be empty

create_handoff.description: Write the handoff for the version the person approved, so Koda can build it without guessing: the design system, sitemap, user flows, every page and component (by their data-design-id), interactions, responsive rules, accessibility, assets and the decisions made. The brief, the feedback's outcome and the approved preview's version and address are added for you. It only works once the person has approved a version.

accessibility.description: Contrast, focus order, labels, motion and touch target rules

assets.description: Images, icons and fonts: the name, the kind and where each comes from

components.description: Each reusable component: its data-design-id in the preview, name, what it is, and its states (hover, empty, error, loading)

decisions.description: The design decisions that were made and why

colors.description: Every colour: its name, its value (hex) and what it is used for

typography.description: Every text style: its role, font, size/line height and weight

interactions.description: What happens when something is used: its target, the trigger and the result

pages.description: Every page of the approved preview: its path, purpose, and the data-design-id of each section top to bottom

responsive.description: How the layout changes from a phone to a desktop, with the widths

sitemap.description: Every page: its path in the preview, its title and what it is for

user_flows.description: What people do, step by step

create_project.description: Create a new project for the app the user wants built. Call this once, before writing a plan.

backend.description: relay for anything that keeps data on a server, signs people in, stores files or calls paid APIs (Nomi Relay gives it a database, sign-in, storage and functions); drizzle only for an app that brings its own database code. Leave it out for browser-only apps.

description.description: One-sentence description of what it does

stack.description: sveltekit (default: anything with pages and a server or database), react or vue (browser-only apps, when the user asks), astro (content sites), static (a single plain HTML page)

create_reminder.description: Schedule a reminder to fire at a specific future time. Resolve any relative time the user gives ("tomorrow", "in an hour") to an absolute ISO 8601 datetime yourself, using the current date/time and the user's timezone given in your system prompt. Before you set it, make sure you know what it's for, when, and whether it's one-time or repeating (and how often): ask with ask_user for whatever they didn't say, all of it in one card.

label.description: Short human label, e.g. "take a bath"

prompt.description: The instruction the target agent will act on when this fires

recurrence_weekday.description: Required when recurrence is weekly (0 = Sunday)

target_agent.description: Which agent takes this job when it fires

delegate_to_agent.description: Hand the user's request to a specialist. The specialist sees this conversation, takes it over right away and answers the user itself, so don't write a reply of your own when you hand off. Use this only when the request genuinely needs a specialist; answer anything else yourself. Available specialists: money, reminders, workspace, health, personality, planning, coding, inspector, design.

task.description: What the user wants from the specialist, with any details from this conversation it needs

delete_file.description: Delete a file from the project.

docs_append.description: Add text to the end of a Google Doc.

docs_create.description: Create a new Google Doc, optionally with text.

drive_search.description: Find files in the user's Google Drive by name. Returns id, name, type and link. Use it to get the id of a Sheet or Doc.

edit_file.description: Change part of a file: replace old_string (copied exactly from the file, with enough lines around it to be unique) with new_string. Set replace_all to change every occurrence.

edit_reminder.description: Change a reminder's title, time, repeat or notes.

find_tools.description: Search every tool the crew can be given, by what a task needs (e.g. "track my spending", "send an email"). Returns the best matches with what each does, whether you have it (granted), and which crew members have it (carried_by). It only informs: you can still call only the tools you were given.

limit.description: How many tools at most (default 8, up to 20)

query.description: A few words about the task or the tool you're looking for

gmail_draft.description: Save an email as a Gmail draft (not sent). The default for writing email.

reply_to_message_id.description: Gmail message id to reply to (threads the email).

subject.description: Leave empty when replying to keep the thread's subject.

gmail_read.description: Read one Gmail message in full (headers and plain-text body).

gmail_search.description: Search the user's Gmail with Gmail search syntax (from:, subject:, newer_than:7d, has:attachment, ...). Returns id, from, subject, date and a snippet for each.

gmail_send.description: Send an email from the user's Gmail. Only when they clearly asked to send; they approve it in chat first.

reply_to_message_id.description: Gmail message id to reply to (threads the email).

subject.description: Leave empty when replying to keep the thread's subject.

hevy_body_measurements.description: The person's body measurements in Hevy (weight, body fat, sizes), newest first, 10 a page.

hevy_create_exercise.description: Create a custom exercise in Hevy.

hevy_create_routine.description: Create a routine (a workout plan) in Hevy.

rep_range.description: A target range like 8-12 instead of fixed reps.

folder_id.description: From hevy_routine_folders; empty puts it in My Routines.

hevy_create_routine_folder.description: Create a routine folder in Hevy.

hevy_exercise_history.description: Every logged set of one exercise (for progress), optionally between two dates (ISO 8601).

hevy_find_exercises.description: Find exercises (Hevy exercise templates, built-in and custom) by name and/or muscle group. Returns their ids.

muscle_group.description: e.g. chest, quadriceps, lats, shoulders, biceps, hamstrings, glutes, abdominals, cardio.

query.description: Part of the name, e.g. "bench" or "squat".

hevy_log_body_measurement.description: Log body measurements for a day in Hevy (an existing day is updated, keeping what isn't given).

hevy_log_workout.description: Log a finished workout in Hevy.

rpe.description: Rate of perceived exertion from 6 to 10 (e.g. 7.5, 8, 8.5, 9).

hevy_routines.description: The person's Hevy routines (workout plans), 10 a page.

hevy_update_routine.description: Replace a Hevy routine with this version (read it first and send it back whole).

rep_range.description: A target range like 8-12 instead of fixed reps.

hevy_update_workout.description: Replace a Hevy workout with this version (read it first and send it back whole).

rpe.description: Rate of perceived exertion from 6 to 10 (e.g. 7.5, 8, 8.5, 9).

hevy_workout_changes.description: Workouts added, changed or deleted in Hevy since a time (ISO 8601).

hevy_workout_count.description: How many workouts the person has logged in Hevy.

hevy_workouts.description: The person's Hevy workouts, newest first, 10 a page, with exercises and sets.

list_background_tasks.description: List active and recent background tasks in this chat session, with their status and output.

list_budgets.description: List the user's monthly budgets with how much of each is spent this month.

list_connected_tools.description: List the tools on the MCP servers the person connected (visual references, moodboards, their own design tools), each with its server and inputs. Call it before use_connected_tool.

list_files.description: List the project's stack and every file in it, with sizes.

list_personality_versions.description: List your past personality descriptions, most recent first, so you can decide what to roll back to.

list_recent_agent_activity.description: List recent and currently active background delegations for this chat session.

list_records.description: List the records you saved in one collection, newest first.

list_tables.description: List the tables in the app's database, with roughly how many rows each has.

source.description: Which database: the published app's (production, the default) or the development one.

list_transactions.description: List the user's most recent transactions, optionally filtered by category.

limit.description: Max number of transactions to return

log_transaction.description: Record money the user spent or received (e.g. "I spent 45,000 on lunch", "got my salary, 8 million", or a receipt). For a receipt or a purchase of several things, put each line in `items`. Records only; it never moves money.

amount.description: The total, as a positive number (what the receipt says, tax and discounts included). Omit to use the sum of the items.

category.description: Lowercase category, e.g. food, transport, groceries, salary

description.description: What it was, e.g. the shop or the source of the income

items.description: The lines of a receipt or purchase

amount.description: The line's total; defaults to quantity × unit_amount

category.description: Only when this line belongs to another category than the transaction

occurred_at.description: ISO 8601 date or time; omit for now

make_file.description: Make a file for the person and put it in the chat: a CSV or spreadsheet from rows, or a text, Markdown or JSON file from text. Use it when they ask for a file, an export or a download ("put this in a spreadsheet", "make me a CSV of May's spending"). Give it a short name with the right extension, a one-line summary of what's in it, and the ids of the attachments it was made from. It tells the person the file is being made and shows it when it's ready.

content.description: For txt, md and json: the file's text.

name.description: The file's name with its extension, e.g. spending-may.csv.

replaces.description: The id of an earlier file this one is made again to replace.

rows.description: For csv and xlsx: the table, header row first; each row is a list of cells.

sources.description: Ids of the attachments it was made from.

summary.description: One line on what's in the file.

post_crew_note.description: Pin a short note to this chat's crew notes, which every crew member working here reads: a fact or decision the others should keep to ("Budget is 5 million rupiah", "They want the site in Indonesian", "Logged the receipt, don't log it again"). One fact per note; not for chatting with the person.

propose_directions.description: Propose two to four clearly different design directions for the person to choose from, each with what it looks like, why it fits the brief, its trade-offs, colours, fonts and layout. It saves them as a new version and shows the person the choice. Call it again with the whole set (same ids for the directions you keep) when they ask for changes.

directions.description: Clearly different directions: different colours, fonts and layout, not variations of one

id.description: A short stable slug, lowercase with dashes; keep it when you refine the direction

imagery.description: Photos, illustration or none, and their style

recommended.description: true on the one you would pick

summary.description: What it looks like, in a sentence or two

publish_project.description: Publish the project so it's live on the web (or update the live app with the latest changes). Only when the person asked to publish, deploy, go live or update the live app, or tapped a button saying so: the person approves it first. Publishing takes a few minutes; tell them it started and where it will be.

environment.description: Where to publish: production unless the person named another (a-z, 0-9, -).

query_database.description: Run one read-only SQL statement (SELECT, WITH, TABLE or VALUES) on the app's database. Without read_data access you get the columns, the row count and how many values each column has; the person sees the rows.

source.description: Which database: the published app's (production, the default) or the development one.

read_attachment.description: Read the text of a file the user attached (a document, spreadsheet, slides, PDF, or the transcript or description Nomi made of an image, audio or video). Use it when the file's text in the conversation was cut short, or to read a file from earlier in the chat. Read on from where the last part ended with `offset`.

id.description: The attachment id from its <attachment id="…"> tag.

offset.description: Character to start from (0 for the beginning).

read_design_skill.description:
Read one skill from your design library: what you know about design (Taste Skill is your rulebook), the canvas format, styles and systems to offer as directions, the components Koda builds from and more. Read what a step needs before you do it, and read it again when an older read was trimmed. A skill may name references: read one with reference. Areas (read index:<area> for its skills):
design (1): the canvas format and how you work
taste (10): Taste Skill, your rulebook: house rules, layout, sections, copy, colour, type, checks
styles (21): the anti-slop audit, the design loop and named styles to offer as directions
components (4): the shadcn-svelte component kit Koda builds from
references (2): patterns learned from other libraries and how to use references

Start with:
- taste-core: Read this first: Taste Skill is your design rulebook, and this file gives its nine house rules, the page kinds and what each may carry, the order you work in, the benchmark and the anti-slop principles.
- styles-index: The named visual styles you can offer as directions, one line each (style → suits → look), plus how to pick 2–4 that are clearly different for a brief; read this before proposing directions, then read the chosen style files.
- pen-format: Exactly how to write the OpenPencil scene graph the Design Studio draws: the document, every node type and property it understands, tokens and themes, components, the gotchas, and Nomi's rules for ids and size.
- components-kit: How you build the design system frame the shadcn way: semantic `$token` variables with light and dark values, a radius scale, reusable component frames named `<Component> / <Variant> / <State>`, a pinned state matrix, and instances placed with `ref`.
- taste-check: The checklist you run on your own canvas before saving each version: first screen, screens and sections, edges, pictures, the right things for the kind, system, contrast, copy, contacts and the phone, each line a thing you can see in the frames.
- slop-audit: What makes a design read as AI-made, and the audit you run on your own canvas before you save a version: name each suspect element, ask what job it does, delete what has none, and fix the rest with the system you already chose.
- design-loop: How you work before and between versions: turn the brief into a written spec, lock one system and vary one thing at a time, score each version against a rubric and a target before saving, and borrow principles from references without copying them.

reference.description: One of the skill's references, by name

topic.description: A skill's name, index:<area> for an area's skills, or index for the areas

read_file.description: Read the current content of a file in the project.

read_guide.description: Read one of your coding guides: exact package versions, config files and conventions that are known to work in Nomi. Read the stack's guide before writing a project's first files, the design guide before writing any UI, and the database guide before adding a database. Guides: sveltekit: SvelteKit 3 + Svelte 5: full-stack apps (the default); design: How every project should look: a deliberate modern style, and the generic AI look to avoid; database: Drizzle with Postgres or SQLite, and how the preview runs them (projects not on Relay); relay: Nomi Relay: migrations with row-level security, the nomi-relay client, sign-in, files, live changes and hosted functions (projects on Relay); preview: How Nomi runs the project in the browser, and what can't run there; sandbox: How it differs when the project runs in a sandbox on Nomi's servers; react: React 19 + Vite single-page apps; vue: Vue 3 + Vite single-page apps; astro: Astro 7 content sites with Svelte islands.

read_logs.description: Read what the running app printed (newest last). Without read_logs access you get counts only (lines, errors, warnings); the person sees the lines.

environment.description: production unless the person named another.

lines.description: How many of the newest lines (default 200).

read_plan.description: Read the latest plan drafted in this chat: what was agreed with the person, including their answers on design, pages and data. Read it before you start building and whenever you're unsure what was asked for.

read_preview.description: Read the files of a preview you built in this chat, as they were saved: the newest version unless you name one, every file unless you name a path. Call it before changing a preview, so you change from what is there instead of writing it again from memory.

path.description: One file's path; every file when left out

version.description: The preview version; the newest when left out

read_web_page.description: Read a public web page as plain text, e.g. a link from web_search or one the user shared.

rename_chat.description: Rename this chat. Use it when the person asks you to name or rename the chat; pick a short title (a few words) in their language if they don't give one.

title.description: The chat's new name, a few words.

rename_project.description: Rename the current project or change its title and description. Call this when the user wants to rename or change the title of their company, app, or project.

description.description: Optional updated one-sentence description of what it does

name.description: The new project or company name

request_access.description: Ask to see inside the app: read_logs (what log lines say) or read_data (the values queries return). The person approves; it lasts for this project until an admin turns it off.

reason.description: One sentence on why you need it.

reset_chat_personality.description: Take this chat back to the person's default personality (drops the one set for this chat only).

review_build.description: Check what Koda built against the design that was handed over: it looks for the handoff's colours, fonts and element ids in the project's files and says which are there and which aren't. It can't judge spacing or feel. Checks this chat's project unless you name another.

project_id.description: The project to check; this chat's project when left out

rollback_personality.description: Roll back to a previous personality version. This creates a new version with that version's description rather than deleting anything.

version.description: The version number to restore, from list_personality_versions.

run_background_task.description: Execute a command or operation in the background without blocking this turn. Returns a task_id immediately so you can either start working on another task right now while waiting, or finish your turn and wait while Nomi remains free to work on other tasks. When the background task finishes, it automatically spawns Nomi with the output to review and follow up.

command.description: The command to execute in the background

label.description: Short human-readable description of what this background task is doing

project_id.description: Optional project UUID when the command is for a specific project

timeout_seconds.description: Maximum seconds the background command may run (default 180, max 600)

run_command.description: Run one command in the project's preview (Node, in the user's browser or the project's server sandbox) and get its output: 'npm install', 'npm install zod', 'npm run db:generate', 'npx ...', 'node ...'. One command at a time, no shell operators. Don't start the dev server; Nomi runs it. Do not run 'npm run build' during development.

save_preview.description: Build a preview of one proposed direction as an OpenPencil scene graph (canvas.pen): do not build raw HTML pages. Include design variables ($color-*, typography, spacing), a design system frame (colours, type scale, buttons, form fields, components), and app flow screen frames, with a data-design-id / id slug on each frame, section and component (a lowercase slug, unique in its screen/frame, the same across screens that share the element). A preview can be sent in pieces if large: send calls with finished false, and the last call with finished true, which saves the preview as a new version (describe elements on that last call; what you said about an element before carries over). To change a preview, send the updated canvas.pen (the rest stay as they were, with the same ids; drop a file with remove), and name in resolves the open feedback the new version dealt with.

direction_id.description: The id of the direction this is a preview of

elements.description: What the ids in the pages are, for the ones worth naming

files.description: Every file of the preview, whole: canvas.pen (OpenPencil scene graph). Relative lowercase paths

finished.description: false keeps these files in a draft the person doesn't see yet, to send the rest in later calls; true (the default) saves the version from the last version of this direction, the draft and these files

remove.description: Paths to drop from the last version when this call finishes it

resolves.description: The open feedback this version dealt with: each one's number and, in a sentence, what you changed for it. Leave out feedback you didn't act on

title.description: What this version is, in a few words

save_record.description: Save a record in your own private storage for this user, in a named collection (e.g. "trips", "contacts"). Use it for anything you'll need again later.

search_files.description: Find text in the project's files (case-insensitive). Returns path:line: text for each match.

path_prefix.description: Only search under this folder, e.g. 'src/lib'

set_budget.description: Set (or change) the user's monthly spending limit for one category.

set_month_start.description: Set the day the user's money month starts (1–28), e.g. 25 when they're paid on the 25th. Totals and budgets then run from that day to the day before it next month. 1 is the calendar month.

set_personality.description: Set how nomi talks and behaves. By default only in this chat; other chats keep theirs. Use scope "all_chats" only when the person asks for it everywhere ("in all chats", "from now on", "always", "as my default"): it becomes their default and replaces every chat's own personality.

description.description: A concise instruction describing the personality, e.g. 'Be sarcastic and blunt.'

scope.description: "chat" (default): only this chat. "all_chats": the person's default, in every chat.

sheets_append.description: Add rows after the last row of a table in a Google Sheet (e.g. range 'Stays!A:F').

rows.description: Rows of cell values, e.g. [["2026-03-12", "Ubud Villas", 2850000]].

sheets_create.description: Create a new Google Sheet, optionally with a header row.

sheets_read.description: Read a Google Sheet. Without a range: its title and tab names. With a range in A1 notation (e.g. 'Stays!A1:F50'): the cell values.

sheets_update.description: Overwrite cells in a Google Sheet range with the given rows.

rows.description: Rows of cell values, e.g. [["2026-03-12", "Ubud Villas", 2850000]].

show.description:
Show something in the chat as a view instead of plain text, when its shape helps: items, records, steps, times, numbers, choices. Plain text stays best for explanations and short answers; don't use a view for a sentence or two. Don't repeat what the view shows in your reply; add only what it doesn't say: a view can be the whole reply, or come with a line of text before or after it. Views that ask (suggestions, decision, form, card actions) send the person's answer as their next message. `format` is one of text|number|money|percent|date|date_time (money in whole units, dates in ISO 8601); `tone` is neutral|positive|negative|warning. Views and their fields (? = optional):
- list: several items of the same kind. title?, style?: bullet|numbered|check, items: [{title, detail?, meta?, format?, done?, url?}]
- table: records with several fields each. title?, columns: [{key, label, format?}], rows: [{<key>: value}]
- comparison: a few options side by side across criteria. title?, options: [name], rows: [{label, values: [one per option]}], recommended?: option index, verdict?
- stepper: steps of a process and where it stands. title?, steps: [{title, detail?, status?: done|current|upcoming|failed|skipped}]
- timeline: things in time order (a schedule, a history, an itinerary). title?, events: [{at: ISO date/time or label, title, detail?}]
- card: one thing with its key facts. eyebrow?, title, subtitle?, highlight?: {label, value, format?}, fields?: [{label, value, format?}], body?, link?: {label, url (or an app page like /money)}, actions?: [{label, message}], tone?
- chart: numbers to see at a glance: trends, shares, sizes. title?, chart?: bar|line|donut, labels: [..], series: [{name, values: [one number per label]}], format?
- answer: one result to stand out (a total, a yes/no, a date). label?, value, format?, detail?, tone?
- suggestions: next things the person might ask, to tap. title?, items: [message in their voice] (1-6)
- decision: a choice for the person between 2-5 options. question, options: [{label, detail?, pros?, cons?, recommended?}]
- form: several details to collect at once. title?, intro?, fields: [{key, label, type?: text|textarea|number|date|time|select|multiselect|checkbox, required?, options?, placeholder?, default?}], submit_label?
- link: a page worth opening, as a preview. url, title?, description?, image?, site? (left-out details are read from the page)
- task: work going on in the background. title, status?: queued|running|done|failed, detail?, progress?: 0-1, agent?, eta? (your rough estimate, e.g. "10 min")
- shell: a command and what it printed. command, output?, exit_code?, cwd?
- code: code to read or copy (a snippet, a query, a config). code, language?, file?
- diff: a change to one file, line by line. path, before, after (the whole text before and after the change)
- sources: what an answer leaned on, numbered like the [1] [2] citations in your text. items: [{title, url?, detail?, kind?: web|file}]; a file source may add file_id (the attachment id), pages?: [3, 8] (from 1) and spans?: [{page, label, rects?, total_idr?}] where you know the page you read it on; leave rects out unless you know the box
- selection: several of many for the person to tick (subscriptions to track, items to keep). question, items: [{name, detail?, amount?, selected?}], confirm_label?, per? (what the total is per, e.g. month)
- boundary: something you won't or can't do: say why plainly and offer what you can do instead. title, reason, alternatives?: [{title, detail?, agent?, message? (sent when picked), url?}] (0-4)
- quick_replies: short answers to the question you just asked, one tap each. replies: [answer in their voice] (2-6, a few words each)
- cart: a basket at a store, only with prices you actually read from the store; the person checks out there. title, store, items: [{name, detail?, quantity?, price?, available?, swap?}], delivery?, checkout_url, note? (where and when the prices were read)

spec.description: The view's fields, as listed for that view

show_reminders.description: List the user's upcoming reminders (with ids).

speak.description: Say something out loud in Nomi's voice: posts a recording the person can play. Use it when they ask to hear something or to be answered by voice ("read it to me", "say it", "reply with voice", "send a voice note"), not for ordinary replies. Pass exactly the words to say, written for listening: no markdown, lists or links. The recording is your reply: after it, write nothing, unless something really has to be in writing too (a link, code, an address or numbers to keep), and then write only that.

text.description: The words to say, as they should be spoken.

stop_agents.description: Stop agents that are working, at the user's request. Cancels their running and queued work and any approvals they are waiting on. Use scope "this_chat" for "stop" or "cancel that", "everything" for every agent in every chat, or "agent" with the agent's name or type (e.g. "money", "coding", "planning") to stop one agent.

summarize_budget.description: Summarize the user's spending (not income) grouped by category, optionally since a given date.

update_record.description: Change fields of one of your records (the given fields replace those keys).

update_todos.description: Set or replace your current multi-step task checklist, shown live to the user. Call this again with the full updated list whenever a step's status changes.

use_connected_tool.description: Call one tool from list_connected_tools: its server and tool exactly as listed, and arguments that fit its inputs. The person approves it first. If it fails, carry on without it.

web_search.description: Search the internet for current or factual information you don't already know (news, prices, schedules, facts to check). Returns titles, links and snippets; use read_web_page on a link for the full text. Cite the links you use right after the claim they back, as numbered markdown links ([1](https://…), [2](https://…)), numbered in the order you first cite them; they show as citations with the sources listed under the reply.

query.description: What to search for, as you'd type it into a search engine

write_file.description: Create or overwrite one file in the project. To change part of an existing file, use edit_file instead.

write_files.description: Create or overwrite several files at once (up to 40). Use it to set a project up or add a feature that spans files.

write_plan.description: Write a new version of your plan for this task, before or during a multi-step build. Call this again whenever the plan changes significantly — each call is a new, separately viewable version, not an edit to the last one.

title.description: Short label for this plan version
